:::{#exm-poisson-reg}
#### Poisson regression with one binary covariate

Let $x_1 = 1$ for smokers and $x_1 = 0$ for non-smokers,
and suppose a Poisson regression model for hospitalizations has
$\beta_0 = \logf{0.002}$ and $\beta_1 = \logf{1.5}$,
with exposure measured in person-years.
By @eq-mean-poisson,
the event rates are:

$$
\ba
\lambda(x_1 = 0)
&= \expf{\beta_0}
&& \text{(rate function with } x_1 = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0.002
&& \text{(} \expf{\logf{0.002}} = 0.002 \text{)} \\
\lambda(x_1 = 1)
&= \expf{\beta_0 + \beta_1}
&& \text{(rate function with } x_1 = 1 \text{)} \\
&= \expf{\beta_0} \cdot \expf{\beta_1}
&& \text{(product rule for exponentials)} \\
&= 0.002 \cdot 1.5
&& \text{(evaluate each factor)} \\
&= 0.003
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

For a group of non-smokers followed for $t = 500$ person-years,
the expected number of hospitalizations is

$$
\ba
\mu(x_1 = 0, t = 500)
&= \lambda(x_1 = 0) \cdot 500
&& \text{(mean = rate} \times \text{exposure)} \\
&= 0.002 \cdot 500
&& \text{(substitute the rate)} \\
&= 1
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

and the probability that this group has no hospitalizations is

$$
\ba
\P(Y = 0 \mid x_1 = 0, t = 500)
&= \frac{1^0 \expf{-1}}{0!}
&& \text{(Poisson PMF with mean 1)} \\
&= \expf{-1}
&& \text{(} 1^0 = 0! = 1 \text{)} \\
&\approx 0.368
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

The same follow-up time for smokers gives
$\mu(x_1 = 1, t = 500) = 0.003 \cdot 500 = 1.5$
expected hospitalizations.

:::
